dervis-irab:39-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَغْرَمٍ) The maghram is that a person takes upon himself what is not incumbent on him.
(كِسْفاً) A piece; it is also said to be «كِسَفاً», whose singular is «كِسْفَة», like «سِدْرَة» and «سِدْر».
(مَرْكُومٌ) Placed one part on top of another.

* I'rab:
(أَمْ لَهُ الْبَناتُ وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ) «له» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «البنات» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ولكم البنون» is conjoined to «له البنات».
(أَمْ تَسْئَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ) «تسألهم» is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and a first direct object; «أجرا» is the second direct object. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «من مغرم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مثقلون»; and «مثقلون» is the khabar.
(أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and «الغيب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause «يكتبون» is the khabar.
(أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْداً فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ) «يريدون» is a nominative imperfect verb, the «واو» is the agent, and «كيدا» is the direct object. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ — this is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, which has been pointed out before; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila (relative clause). «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «المكيدون» is its khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of «الذين».
(أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «إله» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «غير الله» is an adjective of «إله»; «سبحان الله» is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); «عمّا» is attached to «سبحان»; and the clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position, because «ما» is either a relative noun or a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle.
(وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفاً مِنَ السَّماءِ ساقِطاً يَقُولُوا سَحابٌ مَرْكُومٌ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «يروا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the «نون», and the «واو» is the agent; «كسفا» is the direct object; «من السماء» is an adjective of «كسفا»; «يقولوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «سحاب» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and «مركوم» is an adjective of «سحاب».
(فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ) The «فاء» is the «fāʾ al-faṣīḥa» (the eloquent fāʾ), because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied sense being: "if they have reached this limit in disbelief and obstinacy, and it has become clear that they will not turn back from disbelief, then leave them until they die upon it". «ذرهم» is an imperative verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; «حتى» is a particle of limit and genitive; «يلاقوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive through an implied «أن» after «حتى» [Translator's note: the source says «مجزوم» (jussive); after «حتى» the verb is normally subjunctive (manṣūb), and the verb here has no visible ending to show either]; «يومهم» is the direct object; «الذي» is an adjective of «يومهم»; «فيه» is attached to His words «يصعقون»; and the clause «يصعقون» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «الذي». «يصعقون» is passive, from the triliteral «صعق» or from the quadriliteral «أصعق», the meaning being that others made them swoon; it was also read «يَصْعَقُون» with the active voice, meaning "they die from the severity of the terrors".
(يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ) «يوم» is a badal (substitute) for «يومهم»; the clause «لا يغني» is in the position of the genitive, through the adverbial's being annexed to it; «عنهم» is attached to «يغني»; «كيدهم» is the agent of «يغني»; «شيئا» is a direct object or an absolute object; the «واو» is a conjunction, «لا» is negative, «هم» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «ينصرون» is the khabar.
(وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذاباً دُونَ ذلِكَ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The «واو» is resumptive; «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «للذين» is its fronted khabar; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun [Translator's note: the source says «كفروا», although the verse has «ظلموا»]; «عذابا» is the postponed noun of «إن»; «دون» is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of «عذابا»; «ذلك» is a demonstrative, genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. As for «ولكن», the «واو» is a conjunction or circumstantial, and «لكن» is a particle resembling the verb, for rectification; «أكثرهم» is its noun, and the clause «لا يعلمون» is the khabar of «لكن».
(وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «اصبر» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «لحكم ربك» is attached to «اصبر»; the «فاء» gives a reason; «إن» and its noun; «بأعيننا» is the khabar of «إنك», i.e. "within Our sight, where We see you and guard you". The plural of «العين» is used because the pronoun is in plural form. «سبّح» is conjoined to «اصبر»; «بحمد ربك» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "joined with the praise of your Lord"; «حين» is an adverbial attached to «سبّح»; and the clause «تقوم» is in the position of the genitive, through the adverbial's being annexed to it.
(وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «من الليل» is attached to «سبّحه»; «سبّحه» is an imperative verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; «إدبار النجوم» is a maṣdar that stands in for the adverbial, and its ruling will come in the section on Benefits.

* Benefits:
What stands in for the adverbial is what is genitive through the annexation of one of the two adverbials to it, after which the muḍāf (the first term of the construct) is omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi is put in its place after its omission. Most often this muḍāf ilayhi which stands in for the omitted muḍāf is a maṣdar, as in «جئتك صلاة العصر» ("I came to you at the time of the afternoon prayer") or «قدوم الحاج» ("at the arrival of the pilgrim"): «صلاة» and «قدوم» are both mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), accusative with the accusative of an adverb of time, because when they stood in for time, the nominal status of time befell them, so they became accusative as it is accusative. The original is «وقت صلاة العصر» and «وقت قدوم الحاج». Of this kind is «وإدبار النجوم», i.e. the time of their setting. Among their sayings is «لا أكلمه القارظين» ("I will not speak to him [until] the two qāriẓs [return]"), the original being «مدة غيبة القارظين» (the duration of the absence of the two qāriẓs): «مدة» was omitted and «غيبة» put in its place, then «غيبة» was omitted and «القارظين» put in its place. It is the dual of «قارظ», who is the one who gathers the «قَرَظ» (with fatḥa on the «قاف» and the «راء»), which is something with which hides are tanned. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "«لا آتيك أو يئوب القارظ العنزي»" ("I will not come to you until the qāriẓ of ʿAnaza returns"), and they are two qāriẓs, both of ʿAnaza, who went out seeking «القرظ» and did not return, and their absence was prolonged.

dervis-irab:1-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطُّورِ) A well-known mountain. It was said that al-Ṭūr is any mountain on which fruit-bearing trees grow, and one on which nothing grows is not a ṭūr. Al-Mubarrad said: "Every mountain is called a ṭūr; but when alif and lām of definiteness enter, it refers to one particular thing."
(مَسْطُورٍ) Consistently written in ordered lines, in arranged letters. In al-Mukhtār: "Al-saṭr is a row of something; one says 'he built a saṭr'. Al-saṭr is also the line and the writing; it is originally a maṣdar and its verb pattern is naṣara; also saṭar with two fatḥas; the plural is asṭār, like sabab and asbāb; the plural of the plural is asāṭīr; and the plural of al-saṭr is asṭur and suṭūr, like aflus and fulūs."
(رَقٍّ) Al-raqq, with fatḥa or kasra, is thin skin on which one writes, and its plural is ruqūq; al-riqq, with kasra, is the owned slave. Al-Rāghib's text: "Al-raqq is anything written on, whether skin or otherwise, and it is with fatḥa on the rāʾ according to the better-known view, though kasra is permissible, as it was read in an irregular reading. As for al-riqq, which is the ownership of slaves, it is with kasra only." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-raqq is the leaf; it was also said to be the skin on which is written the book in which deeds are recorded."
(الْمَسْجُورِ) Filled with water.
(تَمُورُ) It shakes, comes and goes. In al-Mukhtār: "Māra (verb pattern qāla): it moved and went; and from it His saying, the Exalted, «يوم تمور السماء مورا». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it surges with a surging; Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: it tilts over."
(اصْلَوْها) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Ṣaliya bi-l-nār and ṣaliyahā, yaṣlā (verb pattern taʿiba): he felt its heat; al-ṣalāʾ, on the pattern of kitāb, is the heat of fire; and ṣalaytu l-laḥma uṣlīhi (verb pattern ramā): I roasted the meat."
(يُدَعُّونَ) Al-daʿʿ is pushing. It was said to be that the hands are shackled to the necks and the sides are gathered to the feet, and then they are pushed violently on their faces. In al-Mukhtār: "Daʿʿahu: he pushed him (verb pattern radda); and from it His saying, the Exalted, «فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم»."

* I'rab:
(وَالطُّورِ وَكِتابٍ مَسْطُورٍ فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ) The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; they are five oaths, whose response is «إن عذاب ربك لواقع». The first wāw is for the oath and the wāws after it are conjunctions, or each of them is for an oath; فِي رَقٍّ is attached to مَسْطُورٍ or is another adjective of كِتابٍ. (وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ) Conjoined to His saying «والطور», or each of them is an independent oath, and the response to all of them is His saying: (إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ لَواقِعٌ) inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and وَاقِعٌ is the khabar of inna. (ما لَهُ مِنْ دافِعٍ) مَا is negative; لَهُ is a fronted khabar; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and دَافِعٍ is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; this sentence is a second khabar of inna or an adjective of وَاقِعٌ. (يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً) The adverb is attached to وَاقِعٌ, that is, "the punishment will befall on that day", and the negative clause is parenthetical between the operator and what it governs; it was also said that the adverb is attached to دَافِعٍ. The clause تَمُورُ السَّماءُ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and مَوْراً is an absolute object. (وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبالُ سَيْراً) The sentence is conjoined to the clause تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً. (فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, since the speech has the sense of requital, and the implied form is "when what was mentioned occurs, woe to those who deny Allah and His Messenger"; وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ, and commencing with it was permissible because of the sense of supplication it contains; يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverb accusative by وَيْلٌ, with إِذْ an adverb annexed to a like adverb, the tanwīn being a substitute for a clause; and لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ is the khabar of وَيْلٌ. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ) الَّذِينَ is an adjective of الْمُكَذِّبِينَ; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ, فِي خَوْضٍ is attached to يَلْعَبُونَ, and the clause يَلْعَبُونَ is their khabar; the sentence has no position because it is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ. (يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا) The adverb is a badal from يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً or from يَوْمَئِذٍ before it; the clause يُدَعُّونَ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; يُدَعُّونَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; إِلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ is attached to يُدَعُّونَ; and دَعًّا is an absolute object. (هذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِها تُكَذِّبُونَ) The sentence is accusative as the object of an omitted saying, that is, "it will be said to them: this"; هذِهِ is a mubtadaʾ and النَّارُ the khabar; الَّتِي is an adjective, and the clause كُنْتُمْ is the ṣila of الَّتِي; kāna and its noun; بِها is attached to تُكَذِّبُونَ, and the clause تُكَذِّبُونَ is the khabar of كُنْتُمْ. (أَفَسِحْرٌ هذا أَمْ أَنْتُمْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, the implied form being "you used to say of the revelation, 'this is sorcery'; is this sorcery?", meaning: is this thing too, which bears it out, sorcery? and the fāʾ has conveyed this meaning. سِحْرٌ is a fronted khabar and هذا a postponed mubtadaʾ; أَمْ may be munqaṭiʿa (disconnected) in the sense of "rather", because the speech is complete at His saying «أفسحر هذا», and then He said «أم أنتم», that is, "rather, you do not see"; or it may be muttaṣila (connected), that is, "neither of the two is established, so it is established that you have been resurrected and that what you see is true", which is a severe reproach and a dreadful mockery. أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تُبْصِرُونَ the khabar. (اصْلَوْها فَاصْبِرُوا أَوْ لا تَصْبِرُوا سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ) اصْلَوْها: an imperative verb, agent and direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اصْبِرُوا an imperative verb and agent; أَوْ is a conjunction, lā prohibitive, and تَصْبِرُوا an imperfect verb jussive by lā; سَواءٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "your patience and leaving it are equal", and عَلَيْكُمْ is attached to سَواءٌ. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "equal for you are the two things", and Abū Ḥayyān followed him; nothing prevents that, because the sense of equalising contained in سَواءٌ gave it a benefit that justified parsing it as a mubtadaʾ. (إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) innamā: the particle that restrains (kāffa) and the one restrained; تُجْزَوْنَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; مَا is a relative noun, a second direct object, and the clause كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ is the ṣila; kāna and its noun, and the clause تَعْمَلُونَ is its khabar; and the clause innamā tujzawna is a justification of the equality.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in His saying «الذين هم في خوض يلعبون»:
The origin of khawḍ is to be in water; one says "khāḍa l-māʾ", he entered it; then it came to predominate for plunging into falsehood and other things. Lying and rushing into falsehood are likened to a deep pool which the player wades into. One says "khāḍa l-ghamarāt", that is, he plunged into it; "khāḍa fī l-ḥadīth", he went on at length in it; "khāḍa l-jawādu fī l-maydān", the steed frolicked on the field; and one says "he wades through deaths" (yakhūḍu l-manāyā), that is, he throws himself into perils; and "he wades through the night" (yakhūḍu l-layl), that is, he gropes about in it, heedless of terrors. In the language there are nouns on which particular meanings came to predominate, such as iḥḍār (bringing forward), which is general for everything and then came to predominate in use for bringing forward for punishment; the Exalted said: «لكنت من المحضرين». Its parallel among the predominant nouns is dābba, which came to predominate for four-legged creatures, and qawm, which came to predominate for men. The metaphor here is explicit.
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): كِتاب was made indefinite in His saying «وكتاب مسطور» because it is a particular book from among the genus of books, as in His saying: «ونفس وما سواها».
3- Self-imposed constraint (al-iltizām): in His saying «والطور وكتاب مسطور» is the art of iltizām, to which reference has already been made, for the ṭāʾ has come before the wāw of ridf as an obligatory element.

dervis-irab:17-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فاكِهِينَ) Enjoying comfort and delight. Al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ said: fākihīn means admiring what their Lord has given them. In al-Mukhtār: "Fakiha l-rajulu (verb pattern salima), fa-huwa fakih, when he is of good spirit and humorous. Al-fakih is also the arrogant, insolent one. It was read «ونعمة كانوا فيها فكهين», that is, 'insolent', and «فاكهين», that is, 'enjoying comfort'. Al-mufākaha is jesting; tafakkaha means he was astonished, and it was also said, he regretted; Allah the Exalted said: «فظلتم تفكهون», that is, 'you regret'; and tafakkaha bi-l-shayʾ means he enjoyed it."
(بِحُورٍ) Al-ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrāʾ, from al-ḥawar, which is the intense whiteness of the eye in the intense blackness of it.
(عِينٍ) Al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, which is a woman with wide eyes.
(أَلَتْناهُمْ) We diminished them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Alata l-shayʾa altan (verb pattern ḍaraba): it diminished; it is also used transitively, so one says alatahu."
(السَّمُومِ) Fire, because it enters the pores; it is originally the hot wind that penetrates the pores; the plural is samāʾim. Thaʿlab said: al-samūm is the intensity of heat and the intensity of cold in the daytime. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-samūm is by day, though it may occur at night, and al-ḥarr is by night, though it may occur by day. It was said that the origin of al-samūm is from al-samm, which is the outlet of breath, so every aperture is a samm; or from al-samm, which kills (poison).

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ) inna and its noun; فِي جَنَّاتٍ is its khabar, and نَعِيمٍ is conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ. The speech is resumptive, brought to convey glad tidings to the pious; it may also be a continuation of what is said to the disbelievers, to increase their vexation and bring regret into their hearts. (فاكِهِينَ بِما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ) فاكِهِينَ is a ḥāl, and بِما is attached to فاكِهِينَ; مَا is a relative noun referring to the fruits that are in Paradise, that is, "taking delight in the fruit of Paradise"; the bāʾ may also mean "in", that is, "in what He has given them of fruits and other things"; and مَا may also be maṣdariyya. آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ is a past verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; وَوَقاهُمْ is conjoined to the ṣila, that is, "delighting in their Lord's giving and in His protecting them from the punishment of Hell". The wāw may be circumstantial, in which case the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with qad implied according to those who require it to accompany a past verb occurring as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ. عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ is a second direct object. (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The sentence is the content of an omitted saying; هَنِيئاً is a ḥāl or an absolute object, being in the sense of a maṣdar. Full discussion of هَنِيئاً has been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. بِما is attached to كُلُوا or اشْرَبُوا, and the clause كُنْتُمْ is a ṣila; kāna and its noun, and the clause تَعْمَلُونَ is the khabar of كُنْتُمْ. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that the bāʾ be redundant and مَا be the agent of هَنِيئاً, but the redundancy of the bāʾ is not analogical except in the agent of kafā, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected this of him. (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ) مُتَّكِئِينَ is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in His saying فِي جَنَّاتٍ, that is, "being in gardens, reclining", or from the agent of كُلُوا, or from the object of آتاهُمْ, or from the object of وَقاهُمْ; عَلى سُرُرٍ is attached to مُتَّكِئِينَ, and مَصْفُوفَةٍ is an adjective of سُرُرٍ; the wāw is a conjunction, and زَوَّجْناهُمْ is a verb, agent and direct object; بِحُورٍ is attached to زَوَّجْناهُمْ, and عِينٍ is an adjective of حُورٍ. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ)
There are three views on the wāw, which we set out below, then we indicate where the preponderance lies: 1- It is resumptive; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the clause أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ; this is the view of most of the exegetes and parsers. 2- Abū l-Baqāʾ said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, the implied form being "and We honoured those who believed". 3- Al-Zamakhsharī said: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا is conjoined to حُورٍ عِينٍ, that is, "We paired them with the ḥūr and with those who believed", meaning with companions and fellows from among them, as in His saying, the Exalted, «إخوانا على سرر متقابلين», so they enjoy at one time the dalliance of the ḥūr and at another the companionship of their believing brothers. Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "No one imagined that His saying «والذين آمنوا» is conjoined to «بحور عين» other than this man, and it is a non-Arab imagining contrary to the understanding of the Arab", and we do not hesitate to side with Abū Ḥayyān in his rebuttal. The clause آمَنُوا is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ is conjoined to آمَنُوا; بِإِيمانٍ is a ḥāl from ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ, that is, "the offspring being accompanied by faith"; and the clause أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. (وَما أَلَتْناهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِما كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; أَلَتْناهُمْ is a verb, agent and direct object; مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ is a ḥāl; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and شَيْءٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a second object; كُلُّ is a mubtadaʾ and امْرِئٍ its muḍāf ilayhi; in بِما, the bāʾ is a preposition and مَا is relative or maṣdariyya, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to رَهِينٌ, and رَهِينٌ is the khabar of كُلُّ. (وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِفاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ) وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ is conjoined to what preceded; بِفاكِهَةٍ is attached to أَمْدَدْناهُمْ; وَلَحْمٍ is conjoined to فاكِهَةٍ; مِمَّا is an adjective, and the clause يَشْتَهُونَ is the ṣila of the relative. (يَتَنازَعُونَ فِيها كَأْساً لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ) The sentence is resumptive; it was also said to be accusative as a ḥāl from the object of أَمْدَدْناهُمْ. يَتَنازَعُونَ is an imperfect verb and agent, and فِيها is attached to يَتَنازَعُونَ; كَأْساً is a direct object; lā is the lā of generic negation, ignored for its repetition; لَغْوٌ is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is فِيها, and وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ is conjoined to it; commencing with it was made permissible by the negation preceding it. The meaning of "they contend over the cup" is that they pull it back and forth in playful pulling, since the people of this world have a pleasure in that; it was also said that يَتَنازَعُونَ means they hand it to one another. Al-Akhṭal said: "I contended with him over the fine, cool wine, when the cocks had crowed and the time of the night traveller's halt had come."
(وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمانٌ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; يَطُوفُ is a nominative imperfect verb, and عَلَيْهِمْ is attached to يَطُوفُ; غِلْمانٌ is the agent of يَطُوفُ, and لَهُمْ is an adjective of غِلْمانٌ; ka-anna and its noun, and لُؤْلُؤٌ is its khabar, and مَكْنُونٌ an adjective of لُؤْلُؤٌ; the clause كَأَنَّهُمْ is a second adjective. (وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ is a verb and agent, and عَلى بَعْضٍ is attached to أَقْبَلَ
and the clause يَتَساءَلُونَ is a ḥāl. (قالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنا مُشْفِقِينَ) قالُوا is a verb and agent; inna and its noun, and the clause كُنَّا is its khabar, and the clause إِنَّا كُنَّا is the content of the saying; قَبْلُ is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording and not in meaning, and the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; مُشْفِقِينَ is the khabar of كُنَّا. (فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا وَوَقانا عَذابَ السَّمُومِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; مَنَّ اللَّهُ is a verb and agent, and عَلَيْنا is attached to مَنَّ; وَوَقانا is conjoined to مَنَّ, and عَذابَ السَّمُومِ is a second direct object. (إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ) inna and its noun; kāna and its noun; مِنْ قَبْلُ is a ḥāl; the clause نَدْعُوهُ is the khabar of كُنَّا, and the clause كُنَّا is the khabar of إِنَّا; inna and its noun; هُوَ is a separating pronoun or ʿimād; الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ are two khabars of inna; and the clause إِنَّهُ is a justification with no position.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted, concise simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mujmal): in His saying «كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون» there is a tashbīh mursal mujmal. He likened the youths to pearls hidden in their shells, because it is finer and purer, or because it is stored away and only what is precious and highly valued is stored. The ṣadaf of the pearl is its covering, the singular being ṣadafa, like qaṣaba and qaṣab.

* Benefits:
When the lā of generic negation is repeated, five forms are permissible with it: 1- Both nouns are indeclinable, on the basis that it operates the operation of inna in both, as in: لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله.
2- Both are nominative, on the basis that it is ignored, so what follows it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in: لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم. And the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
ماذا تقول لأفراخ بذي مرخ ... زغب الحواصل لا ماء ولا شجر
(What will you say to the chicks in Dhū Marakh, with downy crops, where there is no water and no tree?)
3- The first is indeclinable on the fatḥa and the second nominative, as in the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib:
لا خيل عندك تهديها ولا مال ... فليسعد النطق إن لم تسعد الحال
(You have no horses to give as gifts and no wealth; so let speech help, if circumstance does not.)
4- The first nominative and the second indeclinable on the fatḥa, as in:
فلا لغو ولا تأثيم فيها ... وما فاهوا به أبدا مقيم
(There is no idle talk and no sinning in it, and what they utter there is forever abiding.)
5- The first indeclinable on the fatḥa and the second accusative, by conjunction upon the position of the noun of lā, as in:
لا نسب اليوم ولا خلة ... اتسع الخرق على الراقع
(No lineage today and no friendship; the tear has grown wider than the patcher can mend.)

dervis-irab:29-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الكاهن) The one who claims to report the truth by way of incantations; al-kahāna is the attribute of the kāhin (soothsayer).
(نَتَرَبَّصُ) Tarabbuṣ is waiting for a thing, for a change of its state into its opposite.
(الْمَنُونِ) Fate and death, from manna-hu when he cut it, because death is a cutter; and its rayb (misgivings) are the events that cause misgiving when they come. He said:
تربص بها ريب المنون لعلها ... سيهلك عنها بعلها أو سيجنح
(Wait out the misfortunes of fate for her; perhaps her husband will perish and leave her, or he will incline away.)
(أَحْلامُهُمْ) Their minds. Aḥlām is the plural of ḥilm, which is the forbearance to which reason and wisdom call. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-ḥilm, with kasra, is deliberateness and intellect; the plural is aḥlām and ḥulūm; and from it «أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا»."
(الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ) The plural of al-musayṭir, who is the overpowering, dominating one, from sayṭara ʿalayhi when he watched over him and guarded him or subdued him. Abū ʿUbayda related "sayṭarta ʿalayya" when you take me as a servant. No noun of the pattern mufayʿil has come in the speech of the Arabs except five words:
muhaymin, muḥaymir, mubayṭir, musayṭir and mubayqir; muḥaymir is the name of a mountain and the rest are names of agents. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "Al-musayṭir and al-muṣayṭir is the one set over a thing to supervise it, to look after its property and to record its work; its origin is from al-saṭr, because books are written in lines (yusaṭṭar)."

* I'rab:
(فَذَكِّرْ فَما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكاهِنٍ وَلا مَجْنُونٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ذَكِّرْ is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, implied "أنت"; the fāʾ gives the reason; مَا is the Ḥijāzī negative and أَنْتَ is its noun. As for بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ, this preposition and its genitive noun may be attached to the sense of negation contained in مَا, in which case the bāʾ is causal, which is the highest of the views, and the meaning is "soothsaying and madness are negated from you by reason of the favour of your Lord upon you", as you say "I am not in straitened circumstances, thanks (bi-ḥamd) to Allah and His enrichment" [Translator's note: the source reads «بحمد بالله»; «بحمد الله» is evidently intended]. Abū l-Baqāʾ said that the phrase with the bāʾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and its operator is بِكاهِنٍ or مَجْنُونٍ, the implied form being "you are not a soothsayer nor a madman, while accompanied by the favour of your Lord"; on this it is an inseparable ḥāl and the bāʾ is of accompaniment. It was also said the bāʾ is for the oath and نِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ is what is sworn by, interposed between the noun of مَا and its khabar, so it is attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is "أقسم", with the response omitted, the implied form being "By the favour of your Lord, you are not a soothsayer nor a madman"; and this is the weakest of them. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ) أَمْ is munqaṭiʿa in the sense of "rather", and it is mentioned here fifteen times, all of them binding arguments to which the addressees have no answer. يَقُولُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb; شاعِرٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ is an adjective of شاعِرٌ, and بِهِ is attached to نَتَرَبَّصُ; رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ is a direct object. (قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا فَإِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ) قُلْ is an imperative whose agent is latent, implied "أنت"; تَرَبَّصُوا is an imperative indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; the fāʾ gives the reason for the command, whose intent is threat; inna and its noun; مَعَكُمْ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ is the khabar of إِنِّي; and the clause تَرَبَّصُوا is the content of the saying. (أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلامُهُمْ بِهذا أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ) أَمْ is a conjunction in the sense of "rather", and what was said of it has gone before; تَأْمُرُهُمْ is an imperfect verb with a fronted direct object; أَحْلامُهُمْ is the agent, and بِهذا is attached to تَأْمُرُهُمْ; أَمْ is a conjunction, هُمْ a mubtadaʾ, قَوْمٌ the khabar, and طاغُونَ an adjective. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُ بَلْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) تَقَوَّلَهُ is a past verb with a direct object, and the agent is latent, implied "هو". (فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ مِثْلِهِ إِنْ كانُوا صادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is, "if they say he fabricated it, that is, invented it, then let them bring"; the lām is the lām of command, and يَأْتُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command, the wāw being the agent; بِحَدِيثٍ is attached to يَأْتُوا, and مِثْلِهِ is an adjective of حَدِيثٍ; إِنْ is conditional, and kāna with its noun and khabar; the apodosis of إِنْ is omitted, indicated by what precedes, that is, "if they are truthful in this saying, let them bring". (أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ is attached to خُلِقُوا; and أَمْ هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. (أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بَلْ لا يُوقِنُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded. (أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمْ هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ) The adverb is attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar, and خَزائِنُ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ the khabar. (أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ) لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and سُلَّمٌ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يَسْتَمِعُونَ is an adjective of سُلَّمٌ, and فِيهِ is attached to يَسْتَمِعُونَ. فَلْيَأْتِ: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being "if they claim that, let ... come"; the lām is the lām of command and يَأْتِ is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ is the agent, بِسُلْطانٍ is attached to يَأْتِ, and مُبِينٍ is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا» there is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), for the commanding is attributed to the minds. The Arabs used to pride themselves on their intellects, so Allah disparaged them in that they did not yield for them knowledge of truth and falsehood. It may be considered an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) if likening is intended, and every majāz ʿaqlī may be an istiʿāra makniyya, but not conversely.
2- In His saying «نتربص به ريب المنون» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), for rayb was applied to events, and rayb is doubt; events were likened to doubt because they neither last nor remain in one state.
